messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT detected: us-west inference cluster latency SLO breach. p95=820ms, p99=3.2s (SLO p99 <= 1.5s). Streaming tail spikes and intermittent stalls reported. Auto-run diagnostics attached.

morgan (oncall): saw alerts at 12:03 PDT, jumping p99 from ~1.1s to 3.2s. Dashboard shows spikes correlate with increased KV cache evictions and paging rate. Marking P1 and paging on-call. :eyes:

anya (sre): confirming. I can see a prefill surge on the KV-prefill metrics starting ~12:01. Prefill ops bumped ~6x, decode ops steady. Looks like prefill vs decode imbalance -> KV slab fragmentation -> more paging to disk.

morgan (oncall): any active deploys?

devin (runtime): no user-facing deploys in the window. There was a scheduled quantization roll for a canary model at 11:50 but it targeted a different region. I will pull logs for prefill/decode counters.

sam (platform): checking infra autoscale / node churn. Nothing weird on node count; but disk io on some shards shows elevated wait (iowait). Could be hot shards due to fragmentation.

anya (sre): customer-impact: streaming clients saw stalls and long tails. Support flagged 8 customers with >5s stalls in the window. No total outages but degraded UX.

morgan (oncall): immediate mitigation options? list please.

devin (runtime): quick mitigations we can do now:
- enable prefill throttling knob for the region (reduce prefill concurrency)
- temporarily increase KV eviction aggressiveness to free contiguous slabs (risk: more misses)
- route new streaming sessions to another region (us-east) while we stabilize
- enable decode-priority path to favor decode over prefill for live traffic

anya (sre): I propose this order: 1) throttle prefill, 2) route new sessions away, 3) enable eviction tweak if still high.

morgan (oncall): do it. start with prefill throttle. Devin, can you patch the dynamic config?

devin (runtime): applying prefill throttle (dynamic flag: kv.prefill.max_concurrency=64 -> 16) now.

incident-bot: config-change: kv.prefill.max_concurrency updated to 16 by devin at 12:11:23 PDT.

devin (runtime): also toggled kv.prefill.adaptive_backoff=true to reduce bursty prefill retries.

morgan (oncall): product-support, notify affected customers with an initial note that we are investigating latency and may re-route traffic for improved stability.

product-support: drafting message. will include ETA and mitigation steps.

anya (sre): observing metrics: within 90s of throttle, prefill rate down ~70%, eviction rate immediate drop, paging ops/sec reduced. p95 improved to ~520ms but p99 still ~1.6s (close to SLO). streaming stalls reduced but tail still elevated.

morgan (oncall): next: traffic routing. sam, can you start a gradual reroute of new sessions to us-east and apply a 20% traffic shift to avoid sudden burst?

sam (platform): starting gradual reroute using routing config (route-policy us-west -> prefer us-east for new sessions). Applying 20% shift now.

incident-bot: routing-change: route-policy updated by sam at 12:15:05 PDT.

anya (sre): after 10 minutes of 20% reroute, p99 at 12:25 = 1.3s. good improvement. keep monitoring.

devin (runtime): dug into KV metrics: slab occupancy distribution is very fragmented on shards 3/7/12. Prefill allocation pattern shows many small allocations <256B, leaving free holes. The allocator then starts paging larger segment requests. Suggest run slab-defrag job on those shards during low traffic or shrink slab size.

morgan (oncall): can we run a targeted slab defrag background job with safe CPU cap? I want low-risk operations.

devin (runtime): yes. I'll kick off background defrag with --max-cpu=10% and --rate-limit to avoid IO spikes. Running against shard 3 and 7 first. Command:```\n./kv-slab-defrag --shards=3,7 --max-cpu=10 --rate-limit=50ops/s --dry-run=false\n```\nStarting now.

incident-bot: job-start: kv-slab-defrag on shards 3,7 initiated by devin at 12:28:47 PDT.

anya (sre): defrag progress looks healthy. paging ops down another ~40% after initial pass. p99 now stable ~1.0s. streaming stalls reduced to near baseline.

product-support: sent customer notification with mitigation steps and ETA for full remediation. Received quick replies from two customers confirming improvement.

morgan (oncall): good. we'll keep mitigation window open for 2 hours and continue monitoring. I'm going to start handoff to anya in 30 minutes. Anything else to run?

devin (runtime): one more thing: logs show a small cohort of traffic using a legacy prefill path that doesn't respect the new adaptive backoff. I'll open a bug and push a hotfix to gate that path. For now we can apply an ingress rule to throttle that cohort by header.

morgan (oncall): do it. please add the ingress throttle and the bug link here.

devin (runtime): ingress rule applied: `header X-Client-Version` pattern match legacy -> rate-limit 10r/s. Bug created: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-1973 (hotfix scheduled).

anya (sre): notes for handoff:
- incident root cause: KV slab fragmentation triggered by prefill surge -> increased paging -> tail latency/p99 breach and streaming stalls.
- mitigations applied: prefill throttled, adaptive backoff enabled, 20% traffic reroute to us-east, targeted slab-defrag on shards 3/7, ingress throttle for legacy cohort.
- current status: p95 ~480ms, p99 ~1.0s, paging ops down 65% from peak, eviction rate normalized.
- customer impact: 8 customers reported stalls >5s at peak; support notified and two customers confirmed improvement.
- follow-ups: schedule slab defrag for remaining affected shards off-peak; root-cause fix for legacy prefill path (INF-1973); consider allocator improvements to reduce fragmentation; add alert to detect prefill/decode imbalance earlier.

morgan (oncall): handing off to anya. I'll be reachable if needed. Handoff time 12:45 PDT. :white_check_mark:

anya (sre): taking over. I'll continue monitoring and coordinate long-term remediations. Thanks team.

morgan (oncall): ack, thanks.

incident-bot: incident-status: mitigated -> monitoring. duration so far 0h50m.

devin (runtime): sample diagnostic commands run during triage for ops notes:
```\n# check eviction & paging counters
curl -s http://metrics.local/kv/shard/3 | jq '.evictions, .paging_ops, .prefill_rate, .decode_rate'

# run slab defrag (already executed)
./kv-slab-defrag --shards=3,7 --max-cpu=10 --rate-limit=50ops/s

# routing change (partial)
kubectl apply -f - <<EOF
apiVersion: infra/v1
kind: RoutePolicy
metadata:
  name: us-west-fallback
spec:
  new_session_split: { us-east: 20, us-west: 80 }
EOF
```

anya (sre): saving this thread into the incident runbook and creating a post-incident follow-up doc. I'll include timeline, graphs, and the INF-1973 tracker.

product-support: will send a short follow-up note to customers at end of maintenance window summarizing mitigation and next steps.

morgan (oncall): excellent. closing active mitigation window in 90m unless regression. :thumbsup:
